title: Egyptian Nabonassar Era Calendar
intro: The Egyptian Nabonassar era is an ancient-style 365-day calendar used for astronomical and historical reckoning. Twelve equal months are followed by five extra days; no leap day is added.
summary: Twelve 30-day months and five extra days, every year.
epoch: This model begins with 1 Thoth, year 1 of Nabonassar, corresponding to 26 February 747 BCE in Julian reckoning. Its epoch is a chronological convention, not the earliest Egyptian calendar.
year_rule: Every year has twelve thirty-day months: 12 x 30 = 360 days. Five additional days complete 365. Without a leap day, the calendar drifts relative to the seasonal solar year.
bar_highlight: FIVE EXTRA DAYS COMPLETE THE YEAR
after_note: The five days after Mesore are separate from the regular thirty-day months. They keep the year at 365 days but cannot prevent seasonal drift.
history: Ancient Egyptian civil reckoning used a consistent 365-day year. The Nabonassar era was also used as an astronomical chronological reference. Because the solar seasons run slightly longer than 365 days, the calendar gradually moves through the seasons.
limits: This is the Nabonassar-era wandering year, not the later Coptic leap-year calendar, nor a universal reconstruction of every ancient Egyptian local or royal dating practice.
